page: Microsoft Azure D128nlds_v6 is a high-density, compute-oriented instance belonging to the Dnldv6 family, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It runs on 64-bit x86 Intel dedicated processors, providing 128 virtual cores without hardware GPU accelerators. Unlike traditional general-purpose instances that maintain a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, this low-memory variant supplies 256 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-core balance with 2.0 GB per vCPU.

A core physical differentiator is the inclusion of 7,560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. This extensive direct-attached NVMe disk space caters to workloads requiring high-bandwidth temporary data buffering, transient databases, or rapid localized read and write pipelines without reliance solely on remote storage. The platform additionally retains compatibility with Azure Premium Storage volumes for persistent backend disks.

The hardware configuration emphasizes multithreaded compute throughput and localized NVMe storage density while reducing allocated RAM per core. This reduced memory footprint provides a qualitative cost efficiency advantage over full-memory configurations by eliminating excess memory overhead for CPU-bound applications. The primary tradeoff is the constrained 2 GB per vCPU, which restricts the instance from hosting massive in-memory databases or memory-heavy enterprise analytics.

Given its dense 128 vCPU topology and generous NVMe disk pool, the instance is targeted toward large-scale computational processing. Primary workload fits include distributed software compilation, media transcoding clusters, intensive parallel data transformation pipelines, continuous integration build farms, and high-throughput web service tiers relying on fast local scratch cache.
description: Microsoft Azure D128nlds_v6 is a virtual machine within the Dnldv6 series, powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 128 vCPUs and 256 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-skewed 2 GB per vCPU allocation that minimizes unneeded RAM overhead for processing-intensive operations. A prominent feature is its integrated local NVMe SSD storage capacity of 7,560 GB, providing fast, localized scratch disk space alongside Premium Storage support. It operates without hardware GPU accelerators. With its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU distribution, this server delivers favorable cost efficiency for tasks requiring substantial multithreaded compute capacity and rapid local ephemeral storage without incurring the costs of standard 1:4 memory allocations. The instance fits parallel batch processing, CI/CD pipelines, distributed build systems, large web serving fleets, and high-throughput data parsing workloads where local caching is required.
